requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: The new collector rejects any data type whose symbol has no source declaration (`type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`) and reports MsgPack021 instead. A type from a referenced assembly (Project A) is metadata-only, so it always hits this branch. The central acceptance criterion is therefore unmet: no formatter is emitted 'even when T is declared in a referenced assembly'. The user's partial class is left without Serialize/Deserialize, so the build fails with CS0535. The README section added by this change advertises exactly this scenario. Ledger L11 records that TypeCollector skips metadata types for [MessagePackObject] analysis. It does not cover this new opt-in feature, whose requirement explicitly demands referenced-assembly support.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.FormatterIsGeneratedForTypeFromReferencedAssembly. ProjectA is emitted to a PE image and referenced via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. On head the generator reports MsgPack021 and the output compilation has CS0535 errors, so the test fails.

findings.claim: When no surrogate is given, the collector always uses CreateContractlessMembers, which serializes every public read-write member under its name. Any MessagePack attributes on T are ignored: [MessagePackObject], [Key] and [IgnoreMember], and also [DataContract]/[DataMember]. The requirement (from the maintainer comment) says that if T carries such attributes they are honoured, and contractless applies only when there is no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject]. With this change an [IgnoreMember] member of T is still serialized, and [Key] indices and DataMember names are not used for the wire format.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.MessagePackAttributesOnDataTypeAreHonoured. The generated source for CustomMyObjectFormatter references the [IgnoreMember] property 'Secret' on head.

findings.claim: The new collector rejects every formatted type that comes from a referenced assembly, which is the core scenario of REQ-2129. The data-type guard contains `|| type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`, and that is always true for metadata symbols. So `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>` produces MsgPack021 and no generated body, and the user's partial class then fails with CS0535. Ledger L11 covers only the existing TypeCollector path for ordinary types. It does not cover this new opt-in feature, whose acceptance criterion explicitly requires `T` to be declared in a referenced assembly.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterReferencedAssemblyTests.FormatterIsGeneratedForTypeFromReferencedAssembly. It builds ProjectA (no MessagePack reference) into a metadata image, references it from ProjectB, runs MessagePackGenerator, and asserts no MsgPack021 and no compile errors. On head it reports MsgPack021 and CS0535.

hunches.claim: The new attribute class is public and unsealed, and its `Type? SurrogateType` uses a nullable annotation. Annotations targets netstandard2.0 or netstandard2.1 or older TFMs, so this may break compilation or emit warnings if nullable is not enabled there. It also adds a public API without a PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt entry shown. This is additive and not breaking for existing users.

receipt_plan.detail: Build MessagePack.Annotations for all target frameworks and check for PublicAPI analyzer warnings.

hunches.claim: The GeneratorUtilities hand-written formatter filter now excludes any class carrying GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute. This is a new exclusion only for attributed classes, so existing users are unaffected. However, the filter compares ToDisplayString against a name string, and the collector's ForAttributeWithMetadataName is the only other path. A class that has the attribute but is rejected, for example non-partial, is silently dropped from the resolver while the diagnostic comes from a separate pipeline step. This is opt-in only.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests with an attributed non-partial formatter and check the resolver output and diagnostics.

hunches.claim: The contractless mode orders members alphabetically (Ordinal) and uses string keys. This sets the wire format for the new feature. It also ignores existing MessagePack attributes on T ([MessagePackObject], [Key], [DataMember]) when no surrogate is given. The acceptance criteria say attributes on T must be honoured, and this code never reads them. The result is a different wire format from the default serializer for attributed types.

receipt_plan.detail: Define a type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] properties, and a partial [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class for it. Serialize with the generated formatter and with the default resolver, then compare the bytes: array of ints versus map of names.

hunches.claim: The template change emits `partial class` with no accessibility or `sealed` modifier for user-declared formatters. It also emits the `: IMessagePackFormatter<T>` base list again. The user's declaration already lists the interface, so the base list is redundant. This is legal for partial types, but the generated code must not re-declare accessibility. Generator snapshot output for existing types is unchanged since the non-user branch emits the same text.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing generator snapshot tests to confirm no byte change for non-user formatters, and compile a sample partial formatter.

hunches.claim: Generated formatter for a user-declared formatter uses an ObjectSerializationInfo built with empty constructorParameters and members marked IsWritable even for init-only/required members, and it only requires a public parameterless constructor. For types from other assemblies that enforce invariants in constructors, deserialization of untrusted data bypasses constructor validation by populating all public read-write fields and properties directly. This is not a MessagePackSecurity setting issue, but the generated deserializer does not route through MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep. The depth check is normally emitted by the template, so verify it is still emitted for the IsUserDeclaredFormatter path.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test for a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class over a type with a nested self-referencing member. Confirm the generated Deserialize calls options.Security.DepthStep(ref reader) and reader.Depth--. Also confirm the string-key path emits the same.

hunches.claim: The new collector rejects every type with `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`. That condition is true for any type from a referenced assembly, which is exactly the type this feature targets, so MsgPack021 is reported and no formatter is generated. The new tests only pass if the ExternalTypes reference is a ProjectReference. It is a ProjectReference, so the type still has source declarations in the test setup. A real NuGet or binary reference to Project A will fail.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile ExternalTypes to a DLL and reference it via a metadata reference (or PackageReference). Apply [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] to a formatter for ExternalPerson. Expect a generated formatter, but the current code reports MsgPack021.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode uses a name-sorted order and ignores DataContract/MessagePackObject/Key attributes on T. The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured. No honouring of attributes on T exists in the collector (only surrogate attributes). This is an unmet acceptance criterion.

receipt_plan.detail: Format a type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(1)]/[IgnoreMember] attributes via a generated formatter without a surrogate. Check that the bytes match the keys declared on the type.

hunches.claim: The new MsgPack019-022 diagnostics are reported by the generator through RegisterSourceOutput. The tests, however, use the generator test verifier, and the descriptors are registered in the analyzer's SupportedDiagnostics. The surrogate collector also reuses MsgPack003/005/006 descriptors, so the MsgPack005 expectation is the only evidence of coverage. There is no coverage for the NoDeserializingConstructor diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Remove the parameterless-constructor check in GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect. The tests still pass, so no test covers it.

hunches.claim: The gate `type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty` rejects exactly the case the requirement targets: T declared in a referenced assembly (metadata-only). Every test in the diff uses a same-compilation type (MyType) for diagnostics, and the execution tests hit the same gate only through ExternalTypes. No test in the diff checks the metadata-only path with a negative or an unsupported-type case, and a diagnostic test with a metadata type is missing. A mutation that removes this guard would not be caught.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:68 remove-guard: `|| type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty` -> removed; expected to survive because no test in the diff supplies a metadata-only type with a rejection expectation, and the ExternalTypes success tests would still pass or fail independently of this condition.

hunches.claim: Diagnostics MsgPack019 and MsgPack020 and MsgPack021 are each tested only for one trigger. The MsgPack021 branches for struct/enum/interface kinds, generic types and inaccessible types have no tests; only abstract is covered. The condition `type.TypeKind is not (Class or Struct)`, the accessibility check and the IsGenericType check can be mutated without any test failing.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:67 negate-condition: `!compilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter)` -> `compilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter)`; expected to survive in the analyzer tests because only an abstract public type is used for MsgPack021. The execution tests would fail on this mutation, so this one may be killed, but the generic and TypeKind branches are not.

hunches.claim: The missing-parameterless-constructor path (NoDeserializingConstructor) has no test. Likewise the duplicate-key path (KeysMustBeUnique), missing-[Key] path (MemberNeedsKey) and the `claimedKeys.Add` guard are untested, so removing them would survive.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:76 remove-guard: `if (isClass && !type.InstanceConstructors.Any(...))` -> removed; expected to survive because no test uses a class without a parameterless constructor.

hunches.claim: The surrogate execution test only uses sparse integer keys 3 and 7 and asserts the array header is 8. It never checks that the values land in slots 3 and 7 or that the other slots are nil. The int-key branch `intKey: intKey` vs `members.Count` could be mutated (the string-key branch uses members.Count) and the round trip would still pass. A string-key surrogate path has no execution test at all.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:~143 off-by-one: `CreateMember(target, intKey: intKey, ...)` -> `intKey: members.Count`; the header would become 2 instead of 8, so this is probably killed. However, `StringKey` surrogate mode `(string)key` -> `target.Name` survives because no test uses string keys in a surrogate.

hunches.claim: The test GeneratedFormattersAreRegisteredInGeneratedResolver, plus the change in GeneratorUtilities that excludes attributed formatters from hand-written registration, has no test showing the formatter is not registered twice. A removal of the `!symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...)` guard would survive since the round trips still work.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: `&& !symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...)` -> removed; expected to survive or at most produce a duplicate registration, and no snapshot or test in the diff asserts the generated resolver contents.

hunches.claim: No generator snapshot tests (regeneration) were added for the generated partial class output, and the .tt/.cs template changes are only covered indirectly. Contractless generation also has no test of ordering (OrderBy name) or of public fields, and no test of `[MessagePackObject]`/`[DataContract]` attributes on T being honoured, which the acceptance criteria require. The tests would pass if attributes were ignored.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test with an external type carrying [MessagePackObject]/[Key] attributes and assert its keys are honoured; it fails on head because Collect never reads T's attributes.

hunches.claim: The SurrogateKeysMustNotMixStringAndInt test expects MsgPack005 (reported through the existing analyzer with a compiler error) but the new generator path reports DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys at the surrogate location. The assertion may be satisfied by the analyzer on the surrogate or unrelated code rather than by the new collector. The test does not prove the new code reports it, and also does not assert that no formatter is emitted.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:~128 delete-statement: the `reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(...DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys...)` call; expected to survive if the analyzer already reports MsgPack005 for the Key attributes on the surrogate.

hunches.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter class itself, not its containing types. The template wraps the generated part in `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces`, which re-declares the containing types. A formatter nested in a non-partial outer class (e.g. `class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<X> {} }`) therefore passes MsgPack019 and yields generated code that does not compile (CS0260 on Outer), instead of a clear diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: IsPartial (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:289-295) inspects only formatter.DeclaringSyntaxReferences. FormatterTemplate.tt line 11 emits the formatter inside EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces, so a non-partial containing class causes a compile error in generated code rather than MsgPack019.

hunches.claim: The generator pipeline's predicate accepts only `ClassDeclarationSyntax`, so `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` on a `partial record` or `partial record class` (a class at the type level, but a RecordDeclarationSyntax) is silently ignored. No diagnostic and no implementation are produced, and the user gets only CS0535 with no explanation.

receipt_plan.detail: In MessagePackGenerator.cs:31 the ForAttributeWithMetadataName predicate is `node is ClassDeclarationSyntax`. RecordDeclarationSyntax does not derive from it, so neither Collect nor the diagnostics pipeline runs for record formatters.

hunches.claim: New analyzer diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are registered as Errors (enabled by default) and listed in SupportedDiagnostics. The hunks do not show AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md being updated, so RS2000 release-tracking warnings may fire, and if warnings are errors the generator project build breaks. Users only see the diagnostics once they opt in via the attribute, so this is not a user-facing break.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md contains MsgPack019-022; none of the provided hunks show it.

hunches.claim: Surrogate mode matches members by name and uses the symbol equality of types, but contractless members are serialized with no restriction on types such as delegates or pointers. Collection members in the target type also go through the default resolver, so MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData collision-resistant comparers still apply only if the generated code uses the options resolver. That is not verified here.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the generated formatter output for a type with a Dictionary<string,int> member under UntrustedData. Confirm it resolves via formatterResolver.GetFormatterWithVerify rather than a hardcoded formatter.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: The change generates a formatter for a type that comes from a referenced assembly. A context-free reviewer might see this as conflicting with TypeCollector skipping metadata-only types. Ledger L11 records that skipping as deliberate for implicit analysis, and the new path is an explicit opt-in via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]. It is a separate collector that leaves CollectCore untouched, and the check `type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty` rejects a type that has no source declaration.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] types from referenced assemblies get no implicit formatter or diagnostics. The explicit attribute is a separate opt-in path.

refused.what: Which reading of REQ-2129 is intended (A or B)
refused.why: 3 of 3 independent readers found two readings: A: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for a partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T>, generating a contractless formatter over T's public members (honouring any MessagePack attributes present) in the declaring assembly, with no surrogate type; B: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] with an optional SurrogateType property, where a user-defined surrogate type in Project B mirrors T's shape and keys are mapped by property name, so attribute-based keys and Union settings can be supplied without touching Project A; the requirement says: 'Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:'. Branch A is the change as written; the orientation step could not tie it to one reading (both: The diff adds GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute with a SurrogateType property and GeneratedFormatterCollector emits surrogate-key-based members when it is set, but it also generates a contractless formatter when no surrogate is given, so it covers both readings.).

By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The change is blocked; signing off is not offered until the blocker is fixed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Branch A is the change as written; the orientation step could not tie it to one reading (both: The diff adds GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute with a SurrogateType property and GeneratedFormatterCollector emits surrogate-key-based members when it is set, but it also generates a contractless formatter when no surrogate is given, so it covers both readings.). Closest reading: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for a partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T>, generating a contractless formatter over T's public members (honouring any MessagePack attributes present) in the declaring assembly, with no surrogate type. Code: Generator discovers classes with the attribute, reads T from the IMessagePackFormatter<T> interface, and emits Serialize/Deserialize directly for T's public members, defaulting to contractless when T has no [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract]; no SurrogateType property.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] with an optional SurrogateType property, where a user-defined surrogate type in Project B mirrors T's shape and keys are mapped by property name, so attribute-based keys and Union settings can be supplied without touching Project A. Code: Attribute has a SurrogateType property; generator reads keys/union attributes from the surrogate and emits conversion code between T and the surrogate, which the contractless-only reading would not do.
